note: AWK-82's transcription of the three scanned Long Island String Festival
Association programs, separated from the script that applies it. Read by
transcribe_programs.py --plan, asserted by lisfa-festival-programs.test.ts.
DECIDED AND NEVER REGENERATED, in the sense period-and-forms.json uses and
tilles-center-programs.json repeats. The sources are three image-only scans
in docs/archive/ and nothing derives this file -- there is no parser to
re-run, because the programs are in no spreadsheet and no graph. Re-reading
them means rendering them by eye. So a correction here is the only record of
the correction, and a re-run of the applier must not overwrite one.
LISFA IS A THIRD INSTITUTION, after the Brooklyn lineage and the Long Island
Youth Orchestra. It is also the first FESTIVAL: three divisions -- Elementary,
Junior High, Senior High -- rehearse and perform separately on one afternoon,
each with its own conductor, and Alex played in one division per year.
LISFA IS NOT THE ALL-COUNTY FESTIVAL, and this is the correction worth
reading before anything else here. The space holds three `All-Nassau ...`
Orchestras, abbreviated `All-County ...`, and one Concert that uses one of
them: `1989-01-08 -- All County`. Two of those three Orchestra records were
created and left unused, which makes them look exactly like the records this
transcription wants -- a junior high and a high school division of a Nassau
County festival, sitting empty. They are a DIFFERENT festival's, and the
first pass at this ticket proposed reusing them. Alex corrected it on
2026-09-01. Nothing here touches them, and the two Orchestras below are new.
ONLY THE NASSAU DATE AND ONLY ALEX'S DIVISION BECOME DATA. Each printed
program covers two concerts a week apart -- a Suffolk County one and a Nassau
County one -- and each carries all three divisions' blocks. Alex grew up in
Nassau and never played the Suffolk festival, stated 2026-09-01. What is not
transcribed is recorded per Concert under `alsoOnThePage`, so the scan's full
contents survive in the repository even though seven program lines become
entries: see that key's note for why it is here rather than in Contentful.
NOTHING RESOLVES TO AN EXISTING WORK, which is the opposite of AWK-64 and
worth stating because that ticket's headline surprise was the reverse. All
seven program lines were checked by title against the 659 live Works and all
seven are new; `reuse` therefore holds composers alone -- no hall, no
orchestra, no conductor, no work, no season.
PROGRAM WORDING LIVES ON THE ITEM, NOT ON THE WORK, as in AWK-64.
app/lib/archive.ts resolves an item's display string as
`item.fields.label ?? work.fields.title`, so `label` is the per-performance
string and the place the printed wording goes. Two Works here are titled
against their printed line on purpose -- see `works`.
ONE OF THE TWO PRINTED FORMS NO LONGER SURVIVES ANYWHERE IN THE SPACE. The
Mozart's label was created as the page prints it, `Nachmusik`, and Alex
corrected the label as well as the Work title in the web app on 2026-09-01 --
so the Respighi `Suite #3` is the only printed wording still carried on a
label here. That is a curator overruling the convention rather than the
convention failing, and it is recorded because the rule above still reads as
though both cases hold.
PERIOD AND FORM ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the new Composer and the seven
new Works, for the reason tilles-center-programs.json gives: ADR-0007 puts
every form judgement in period-and-forms.json and lets Form stay incomplete,
so assigning forms here would open a second home for a decided thing. Period
arrives on its own -- work.period inherits from the composer in the AWK-37
sweep. Run imslp_harvest.py --refresh, then seed_period_and_forms.py, after
applying this. The plain harvest re-run is a no-op; it caches the Delivery
read, which cost AWK-64 a wasted pass.
CONDUCTOR SLUGS ARE NULL, following AWK-64 rather than the checklist. All 46
live conductors have conductor.slug unset, no route reads it, and slugging
three of forty-nine would leave a partial state for someone to explain later.
Two pages each, image-only, no text layer. Page 1 is the title page -- the
festival, the annual ordinal, and both concerts' halls, dates and times.
Page 2 is the Nassau County program: the three officers, then the three
divisions in order with their conductors, chairpersons and works.
Added 2026-09-01 as lisfa-92.pdf, lisfa-93.pdf and lisfa-94.pdf, then
recompressed and renamed to the convention above under AWK-82. The scanner
emitted them as lossless RGB bitmaps at 8-10 MB each, the same way it did
the Tilles Center scans; re-encoding each page as JPEG at 2200px brought
them to ~750 KB, a thirteenth, with the typewritten text still sharp --
verified by rendering the junior high block and reading it back, not
assumed from the file size. Do the same to any scan added here.
This machine has no pdftoppm, so rendering means PDFKit -- unlike the
Tilles scans, these pages are not single embedded JPEGs, so there is no
stream to extract. The originals are not in the repository.
Live entry ids this transcription links but does not create. Every one was
verified present on 2026-09-01 before the ids were written down.
COMPOSERS ONLY, and that is not an oversight -- see the top note. Three
Halls, two Orchestras and three Conductors are all absent from the space,
so they are created below rather than reused, and no Season is involved at
all.
THE SORT NAMES BESIDE THE IDS ARE A CHECK, NOT A LABEL.
transcribe_programs.py re-reads each entry and aborts if the id has gone
missing, if it now resolves to a different content type, or if its live
name no longer matches what is recorded here. So correcting a name here is
not tidying; it is the thing that keeps the check honest. The test can only
assert these are non-empty and well-formed, because it has no network.
TWO OF THE SIX ARE AMBIGUOUS BY NAME and the ids resolve the ambiguity:
the space holds two Andersons and three Handels.

handel.why: The plain record, not `Handel, George Frideric (orch. by Mozart)` or `(arr. by Harty)`. The program prints an unqualified `Handel`, and ADR-0005 makes an arranger part of the Work rather than the Composer's identity -- but these two live records predate that and still exist, so the id matters.

anderson.why: Not `Anderson, Douglas`, the other live Anderson, who is a Modern composer with a world premiere in the Brooklyn archive. Fiddle Faddle is Leroy's.

note: Both absent from the space's seven Orchestras, confirmed 2026-09-01. See
the top note for why the two empty `All-Nassau` records are not these.
THE SENIOR HIGH RECORD SERVES TWO CONCERTS, 1993 and 1994. One ensemble,
two years -- the division is the ensemble here, not the roster.
BOTH REGISTERS ARE LOAD-BEARING and they were chosen by Alex on
2026-09-01. `abbreviation` is what the concerts table and a work page
render (AWK-70, AWK-72) AND what an invariant message names instead of an
id, so it has to be short and it has to be distinct: two divisions
abbreviated `LISFA` alike would make the identity app/lib/archive.ts reads
it as useless. `name` is what the concert page renders, so it spells the
festival out and never asks the reader to expand an acronym.
NO COUNTY IN EITHER REGISTER. LISFA ran Nassau and Suffolk divisions and
each program covers both, so `LISFA Nassau ...` was the first proposal.
Alex settled it on 2026-09-01: he grew up in Nassau, never played Suffolk,
and a qualifier guarding against a record that will never exist is
clutter. A Suffolk program would need new records under this decision, and
that is the accepted cost.

note: Three school auditoria, none of them live -- of the 15 Halls in the space
only Tilles Center is on Long Island. These are the first Halls any
committed declaration has created; AWK-64 reused Tilles Center and AWK-59
created Dallas Brooks Hall by hand.
`location` follows the space's format, which is `Town, NY` for the eight
Brooklyn and New York halls and `Institution, Town, NY` where the hall
sits inside a larger campus. A school auditorium named after its school
needs no institution clause, so all three take the short form.
SLUGS ARE HAND-WRITTEN and folded the way ADR-0008 folds a filing name:
`A.G.` loses its periods to `a-g`, the way `Church of St. Ann & the Holy
Trinity` files as `church-of-st-ann-the-holy-trinity`. hall.slug is read by
no route today, and is still swept by AWK-61's whitespace invariant.

hal-oceanside-senior-high-school.name: Oceanside Senior High School
hal-oceanside-senior-high-school.why: The 1993 title page prints the town as `1Oceanside, New York` -- a stray character, not a name. Recorded as `Oceanside, NY` per the space's format; the scan is the record of the typo.

hal-a-g-berner-junior-high-school.name: A.G. Berner Junior High School
hal-a-g-berner-junior-high-school.why: A junior high school hosting the 1994 concert, at which Alex played in the SENIOR high division. The hall's name and the division's are unrelated, and the coincidence is worth one line here rather than a second look later.

note: One per Concert, each conducting their own division's whole block. None is
live -- these are the space's 47th, 48th and 49th.
NO ITEM CARRIES `programItem.conductor` HERE, and that is the field
working as designed rather than going unused: it exists for a Concert
whose blocks had different conductors, and each of these Concerts holds one
division's block under one conductor. The three divisions' conductors on a
single afternoon are three Concerts' worth, not one Concert's.
`slug` is deliberately absent; see the top note.
None. No line on any of the three Nassau programs names a featured
performer, and CONTEXT.md is explicit that section players are recorded
nowhere. The key is present and empty rather than absent so that the
absence is a stated finding rather than a gap in the file.
One, absent from all 263 live Composers on 2026-09-01.
No dates, following AWK-64: the programs print none, and this file records
what the scans say. `period` is absent on purpose -- see the top note. He
has an IMSLP page, so imslp_harvest.py should reach him.

cmp-diamond-david.why: The 1994 program prints composers as `Firstname Lastname` in this block -- `David Diamond`, `Ottorino Respighi` -- rather than the `P. Tchaikovsky` initial form the other blocks use. The forename is the program's, not an inference.

note: Seven, all genuinely new. Slugs are hand-written per ADR-0008 -- the
importer's hashed form is not an address anyone should ship -- and each was
checked against its composer's live slugs and against both patterns
app/lib/invariants.ts rejects: `--` anywhere, and `-[0-9a-f]{6}` at the
end. All seven are free and none matches either shape.
`fiddle-faddle` IS THE NEAR MISS THAT SHAPE IS FOR. Its last segment is
six characters long and five of them are hex; `l` is the only thing
keeping it out of the hashed-slug pattern. Worth knowing before anyone
renames it.
TWO TITLES ARE DECIDED RATHER THAN TRANSCRIBED. AWK-64's rule is that a
new Work keeps the program's wording, and Alex chose the archive's
convention over it in both cases on 2026-09-01. Each `why` says what the
page prints; both printed forms survive on the item label.
`period` and `forms` are absent on purpose. See the top note.

wrk-overture-to-the-messiah.title: Overture to The Messiah
wrk-overture-to-the-messiah.why: Printed as it stands. This is a THIRD Handel record for one oratorio, beside `Messiah` (under the orch.-by-Mozart composer) and `Messiah, Part III` -- which is the archive's existing convention for excerpts, not a duplicate. Nothing here merges them.

wrk-serenade-eine-kleine-nachtmusik.title: Serenade No. 13 in G major, K. 525
wrk-serenade-eine-kleine-nachtmusik.why: The page prints `Serenade (Eine Kleine Nachmusik)`, missing the `t` in Nachtmusik. This transcription created the Work as `Serenade ("Eine Kleine Nachtmusik")` -- the typo corrected, the space's `Title ("Nickname")` shape kept -- and ALEX RE-TITLED IT TO THE CATALOGUE FORM IN THE WEB APP within minutes of it publishing, on 2026-09-01. The catalogue form is what stands, and this file is corrected to match it rather than the reverse: the applier merges and never clobbers, so a declaration left disagreeing would report `DIFFERS, left alone: title` on every future run and slowly read as a bug. The printed form is still on the item label, which is the whole point of the label existing.
wrk-serenade-eine-kleine-nachtmusik.movementsNote: THE FOUR MOVEMENTS ARE THE CURATOR'S, NOT THE SCAN'S, and the distinction is the only reason this key still exists. The page prints one line under the title -- `2. Romanze` -- so this file originally carried no movement list at all, on the grounds that the other three would be invented. Alex added all four from the catalogue in the same web-app edit as the title. That is a legitimate source this transcription does not have, and recording them here keeps the declaration diffable against the space; what it must not do is imply the scan said so. The item's `note` remains the record of what was actually played.

wrk-brook-green-suite.title: Brook Green Suite
wrk-brook-green-suite.why: Holst's sixth work in the archive, beside St Paul's Suite -- its companion piece, and already filed under its own name rather than as a variant.

wrk-fiddle-faddle.title: Fiddle Faddle
wrk-fiddle-faddle.why: Leroy Anderson's third work in the archive, after Sleigh Ride and A Christmas Festival. See this object's note on the slug.

wrk-serenade-for-strings.title: Serenade for Strings
wrk-serenade-for-strings.why: The page prints a bare `Serenade`. Titled `Serenade for Strings` here, matching Barber's and Elgar's live records -- a Tchaikovsky Work addressed as `serenade` alone says nothing, and the four printed movements identify it beyond doubt. Alex chose this over verbatim on 2026-09-01. The label stays `Serenade`.
wrk-serenade-for-strings.slugNote: The slug `serenade-for-strings` is ALSO Barber's. That is legal and intended: ADR-0008 scopes a work slug to its composer, and the entry ids differ -- Barber's is `wrk-serenade-for-strings-eb7ac3`. The build's `work-slug-unique-per-composer` groups by composer for exactly this reason.

wrk-ancient-airs-and-dances-suite-no-3.title: Ancient Airs and Dances, Suite No. 3
wrk-ancient-airs-and-dances-suite-no-3.why: Printed `Ancient Airs and Dances, Suite #3`; normalised to `No.` per AWK-64's rule, which is settled in the space rather than invented here -- Respighi's Suite No. 2 is already live under `ancient-airs-and-dances-suite-no-2`. The printed `#3` survives on the item label.

note: None. No program line here names movements for a Work the archive already
holds -- all seven Works are new, so every movement list this transcription
supplies arrives with its Work under `works`. Present and empty for the
same reason `soloists` is.
Ids, titles and item ids follow AWK-59 and AWK-64: cnc-YYYYMMDD, a title of
'YYYY-MM-DD — <institution>' with an em dash, and pi-YYYYMMDD-N ordered
from 1. Program items are created fresh per Concert and never shared --
app/lib/invariants.ts fails a build where one item sits on two Concerts
more than 14 days apart, because a program item is one performance.
THE TITLES SAY `LISFA`, NOT `All County`. Chosen by Alex on 2026-09-01,
over matching the live `1989-01-08 -- All County`. That concert is a
different festival's and stays as it is; the two are not meant to line up.
NO SEASON ON ANY OF THE THREE, and none is created. ADR-0006 records that
the space's one festival Concert 'carries no season at all and keeps none
-- a one-off guest appearance has no numbered calendar to belong to', and
CONTEXT.md scopes a Season to an institution's numbered concert year. The
festival's own ordinal -- 36th, 37th, 38th Annual Concert -- counts
concerts, not years Alex belonged to, so `sea-lisfa-36` would be a calendar
nothing else uses. The ordinals are in `sourceNote` instead. This is the
first declaration where concert.season is legitimately absent, which is why
the applier had to stop requiring it.
attended is true on all three and satOut is empty on all three: Alex played
every item of his division's block, stated 2026-09-01.
EACH PROGRAM HOLDS ALEX'S DIVISION'S BLOCK ONLY, and this was the choice
with two precedents pulling opposite ways. AWK-59's 1993-07-26 puts the
whole printed program on the Concert and marks the visiting choirs' ten
blocks satOut; the live 1989-01-08 All County Concert holds one division's
five items and nothing else. Alex chose the second on 2026-09-01. The
reason is what satOut means: CONTEXT.md defines it as a Program item Alex
did not play AT A CONCERT HE OTHERWISE PLAYED, and the Elementary and
Senior High blocks are not works he declined -- they are not his program.
participation-checklist.md already flags the 1993-07-26 reading as that
concert's exception, and this keeps it exceptional.
`sourceNote` AND `alsoOnThePage` ARE NOT WRITTEN TO CONTENTFUL, and that is
not an oversight. The content model has nowhere to put a start time, a
festival ordinal, an officer, a chairperson or another division's
repertoire; concert.dateNote exists but qualifies a DATE, and filling it
with a start time would be a misuse that then renders. So the facts are
kept here, in the committed record, and nowhere else -- exactly what AWK-59
did with Keith Glover compering on 1993-07-26.
`alsoOnThePage` IS THE POINT OF DOING IT THIS WAY. Seven of nineteen
printed program lines become entries; the other twelve, three officers,
six conductors, six chairpersons and three Suffolk concerts would otherwise
exist only in a 750 KB image. Recording them costs nothing at build time
and answers the question a later reader will actually have -- what else was
on the page -- without another render. The test asserts all three carry
one, so the key cannot quietly rot into dead weight.
NO ITEM CARRIES `character`. The field holds a non-instrument role -- the
space's honest examples are `Isolde`, `Dancer` and `Filmmaker` -- and AWK-69
cleared the last instruments out of it. Nothing here has a performer at
all. The test asserts no item carries the field.
